draft.title: Quadratic models
card: A quadratic model has the form y = ax² + bx + c, where a is not 0. Its graph is a parabola, a smooth U-shaped or upside-down U-shaped curve.
if a is negative, the parabola opens downwards and its highest point is the maximum. A thrown ball rises to a maximum height, then falls.
if a is positive, the parabola opens upwards and its lowest point is the minimum. This point is called the vertex, as is the maximum point.

To read the answer from a graph, find the vertex. Its y-value is the maximum or minimum value. Its x-value is where that value happens. Example: a ball's height h (metres) after t seconds peaks at the point (2, 20). The maximum height is 20 m, reached after 2 seconds.
draft.remember: The vertex gives the best value (its y) and when or where it happens (its x).

a.q: A graph of a ball's height (m) against time (s) is a parabola with its vertex at (3, 45). What is the maximum height?
a.why: The y-value of the vertex is the maximum value, and y is height here, so it is 45 m. The 3 is the time in seconds when the ball reaches that height, not the height itself.
a.clue: Height is on the y-axis. Which part of the vertex is y?

b.q: Profit P (in dollars) from selling cupcakes at price x dollars is modelled by a parabola with vertex (6, 240) that opens downwards. What price gives the greatest profit?
b.why: The x-value of the vertex is the price at which the maximum happens, so the price is $6. The $240 is the greatest profit, which is the y-value, so it answers a different question.
b.clue: Price is on the x-axis. Which part of the vertex tells you where the maximum happens?
